description: [Independent (Kampala)] Kampala -- Reach A Hand Africa (formerly Reach A Hand Uganda) has launched a year-long, student-focused campaign to promote the well-being of young people across the country. The "Be Better" initiative was unveiled on 12th August 2026 during a school outreach at Namiryango SSS in Mukono.
title: Africa: Reach a Hand Africa Launches 'Be Better' Campaign to Address Youth Well-Being

description: [RFI] Desertification is not the spread of deserts. It is the slow degradation of fertile land - a process that now affects 40 percent of the Earth's land surface and leaves around 100 million hectares of healthy land unproductive every year. As governments gather in Mongolia this week for the UN's Cop17 desertification summit, scientists say restoring soil health is becoming critical for food security, livelihoods and climate resilience.
title: Africa: How Degradation and Drought Are Threatening the Land That Feeds Us

description: [RFI] Singer Angélique Kidjo has become the first black African performer to receive a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame - telling RFI the honour represented "a door opening" at a time of global turmoil.
title: Africa: Angélique Kidjo Says Hollywood Star Is 'For Africa, but Also for France'

title: Africa: Armed Drones Emerge As New Threat to Aid Workers As UN Warns of Rising Violence

title: Africa: Nigeria to South Africa - Deliberate Targeting of Africans Must Stop

description: [OCHA] (Geneva/New York, 19 August 2026): 2025 set another grim record for violence against aid workers, with 907 colleagues killed, injured or kidnapped, the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said today on World Humanitarian Day.
title: Africa: World Humanitarian Day 2026 - Aid Workers Under Fire As Armed Drones Transform War-Making

description: [UN News] A single New York Times article on a disaster generated an additional $500,000 in official aid. That's just one of the findings on the critical role a free press plays in saving lives, according to a new UN report released on Tuesday.
title: Africa: What's Journalism Worth in Disasters and Emergencies? a Lot, Says a New UN Report

description: [The Conversation Africa] Microbial ecology (the study of how tiny microbes interact with each other and their environment) underpins the health of every ecosystem on Earth. The microbes living in soil recycle nutrients, support plant growth and help ecosystems respond to environmental change. In this explainer, microbial ecologist Marc Van Goethem tells us why microbes are critical to human life. They can also provide an early warning if Africa's drylands are approaching ecological tipping points, offering new ways to monitor and
title: Africa: The Soil's Early Warning System - Microbes Can Predict Desertification Before Plants Start to Die

description: [The Herald] The late Cuban leader and Commander-in-Chief Fidel Castro was a revolutionary whose ideas inspired young Zimbabweans to join the liberation struggle and fight for independence, ZANU PF National Political Commissar Cde Munyaradzi Machacha has said.
title: Africa: 'Castro's Influence On Africa Was Infectious'
